newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium hurt and helped by French hauliers strike.
newsitem.headline: Belgium hurt and helped by French hauliers strike.

text.p: The French road hauliers strike, now in its second week, started to squeeze Belgian hauliers on Tuesday with many lorries still trapped and others having to take lengthy detours, a road transport spokesman said.
But ferry operator Stena-Sally Lines reported booming business as trucks headed for Britain were rerouted from the blockaded port of Calais to Ostend.
"The strike is costing hauliers tens of millions of francs," a spokesman for the Belgian Transport Association told Reuters.

"It is impossible to get to Spain by road at all, and getting to Italy you have to detour through Luxembourg, Germany and Switzerland which has a 28-tonne weight limit," he said. "The situation is getting worse hour by hour."
He said the association had advised its members to avoid France, but that some 70 trucks were still trapped in the country.
A spokesman for Stena, however, found it hard to hide his happiness.
"All our sailings are fully booked with freight lorries," he said. "Normally at this time of year they are only half full."
He said passenger traffic was also up -- although that could also be a side effect of the closure of the Channel Tunnel following a fire in one shaft last week.
"We have an extra sailing of the Jetfoil on Saturday," the spokesman said.
